newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea won ends weaker despite intervention fear.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea won ends weaker despite intervention fear.

text.p: The won finished slightly lower versus the dollar on Wednesday despite the fear of a central bank dollar selling, dealers said.
The won stood at 819.30 at the closing bell against the opening of 819.00. It fluctuated in a range of 818.90 to 819.40.
"The market is seriously short in dollars," said a European bank dealer. "The won liquidity was also tight in the money markets, but the demand for the greenback was stronger today."
Due to severe shortage of the U.S. unit, the won is set to fall further unless the central bank intervenes to support it, dealers said.
Dealers said trading would remain cautious on Thursday amid fears of the intervention.
"It's almost certain the central bank would intervene tomorrow, because the dollar is likely to move towards 820," said the European dealer.
A range of 818 won to 820 won is seen with the mid-rate at 819.20 on Thursday. Today's mid-rate was put at 818.70.
